lesson.title: Reading passages B–C: living in new districts

learning_objectives.en: Practise paraphrases, multiple choice and sentence completion.
learning_objectives.vi: Luyện diễn đạt đồng nghĩa, câu hỏi trắc nghiệm và hoàn thành câu.

content.en: IELTS questions may use different words from the article. Compare meaning rather than matching a single word: “nearby services” can be “facilities within walking distance”.
content.vi: Đề có thể thay từ của bài đọc. So sánh nghĩa: “nearby services” có thể được diễn đạt là “facilities within walking distance”.

example.en: made journeys depend on cars = almost every trip required a car
example.vi: phụ thuộc ô tô khi di chuyển = gần như mọi chuyến đi phải dùng ô tô

strategies.en: Eliminate answers contradicted by the text, answers using an unsupported degree (always, only), and answers that mix real facts in the wrong relationship.
strategies.vi: Loại đáp án trái bài, quá tuyệt đối (always, only), hoặc ghép các sự thật đúng thành một kết luận sai.

mini_review.en: Can I locate a specific evidence sentence for every answer?
mini_review.vi: Tôi có tìm được câu bằng chứng cho mỗi đáp án không?

passages.title: Living vertically: what tall housing changes
passages.text:
[A] In many growing cities, the most visible sign of change is upward. Towers of thirty or forty floors now stand where low terraces once lined the street. Supporters argue that building higher is the only realistic way to house more people without spreading the city into farmland. Critics reply that height is not the same as quality, and that a tall building can be crowded, expensive to run and isolating for the people who live in it.

[B] A recent survey of residents in three high-rise estates in the fictional city of Norhaven offers a more detailed picture. Researchers spoke to 420 households, asking how they used shared spaces, how often they met neighbours and how they travelled to work. The answers varied less by the height of the building than by what surrounded it. Residents of towers with a park, a primary school and a bus stop within five minutes’ walk reported the strongest sense of community.

[C] Lifts were a recurring complaint. In the oldest estate, two lifts served twenty-eight floors, and a single breakdown could leave older residents unable to go out. Families with young children said they rarely let them play outside alone because the playground was too far below to supervise. By contrast, a newer block placed a small garden and a children’s room on every fifth floor. Parents there described these spaces as the most valuable feature of the building.

[D] The survey also questioned a common assumption about energy. Tall buildings are often described as efficient because flats share walls and heat is lost more slowly. Residents’ bills, however, depended mainly on insulation and window design. In one estate built with large single-glazed windows, heating costs were higher than in nearby low-rise houses. The researchers concluded that height alone tells us little about energy use.

[E] None of this means that tall housing is a mistake. The city’s planning office now requires new towers to include shared indoor space, at least three lifts for buildings above twenty floors and a public route through the site at ground level. Whether these rules will create stronger communities is not yet known. The researchers plan to repeat the survey in five years, when the first buildings under the new rules have been occupied.

[F] Residents themselves were divided about the experience of living high above the street. Many valued the views, the quiet of the upper floors and the security of a staffed entrance. Others missed the feeling of stepping straight out of their front door into a familiar neighbourhood. Several older residents said they had made more friends in the lift than in their previous low-rise street, which suggests that design can create contact as well as prevent it.

passages.title: Why some new districts feel empty
passages.text:
[A] Visitors to some newly built districts notice the same thing: wide roads, neat lawns and modern apartment blocks, but very few people on the street. Planners have a name for this problem. They call it low street life, and it matters because empty streets feel less safe, shops struggle to survive and residents have fewer chances to meet one another by accident.

[B] One cause is the separation of uses. In many twentieth-century plans, homes were placed in one zone, offices in another and shopping in a third, often linked only by roads. As a result, almost every trip required a car, and the pavements between zones were used by almost no one. Older city centres, by contrast, usually mix homes above shops, schools beside parks and workplaces a short walk away.

[C] Another cause is the size of street blocks. Where blocks are long, people have to walk further to reach a destination, so they are more likely to drive. Short blocks create more corners, more crossing points and more routes to choose from. Studies in several countries have linked smaller blocks with higher levels of walking, although the strength of this link varies with climate and income.

[D] Timing also plays a part. A district is often built in stages, and the first residents may arrive years before the shops, clinics and bus services they were promised. During this period, households form travel habits that are hard to change later. Some developers now open a café, a small grocery and a bus route before the first homes are sold, so that new residents find a working neighbourhood from the start.

[E] Fixing an empty district is slower than designing a lively one. Councils have added ground-floor shops to existing blocks, cut new footpaths through long blocks and allowed markets to use car parks at weekends. Results so far suggest that small changes can help, but only when several are made together and given time to work.

[F] Measuring success is itself a challenge. Some councils now count pedestrians at fixed points several times a year, record how long people stay in public spaces and ask local businesses about their trade. A single busy weekend proves little, because a festival or warm weather can fill a street for a day. What planners look for instead is a steady rise over several seasons, which shows that people have begun to treat the district as a place to spend time rather than only a place to pass through.

exercises.title: Reading extension: Living vertically: what tall housing changes

instruction.en: Answer the questions after reading R-B.
instruction.vi: Đọc bài R-B và trả lời theo bằng chứng.

questions.prompt_en: What type of land could be lost if a city spreads outwards? Write ONE WORD.
questions.prompt_vi: Nếu thành phố mở rộng ra ngoài, loại đất nào có nguy cơ bị mất? Viết 1 từ.
questions.explanation_en: Paragraph A contrasts vertical development with outward expansion into farmland.
questions.explanation_vi: Đoạn A: “without spreading the city into farmland”. Lưu ý: chỉ chép số từ được yêu cầu, không thêm từ không cần thiết.

questions.prompt_en: How many households took part in the survey? Write ONE NUMBER.
questions.prompt_vi: Có bao nhiêu hộ gia đình tham gia khảo sát? Viết 1 số.
questions.explanation_en: Paragraph B explicitly states that researchers interviewed 420 households in three estates.
questions.explanation_vi: Đoạn B: “Researchers spoke to 420 households”. Lưu ý: chỉ chép số từ được yêu cầu, không thêm từ không cần thiết.

questions.prompt_en: In the oldest estate, how many lifts served the building? Write ONE NUMBER.
questions.prompt_vi: Khu nhà cũ nhất có bao nhiêu thang máy? Viết 1 số.
questions.explanation_en: Paragraph C reports that two lifts served twenty-eight floors in the older estate.
questions.explanation_vi: Đoạn C: “two lifts served twenty-eight floors” – viết 2 hoặc two. Lưu ý: chỉ chép số từ được yêu cầu, không thêm từ không cần thiết.

questions.prompt_en: What did the newer block provide on every fifth floor, as well as a garden? Write NO MORE THAN THREE WORDS.
questions.prompt_vi: Ngoài khu vườn, tòa nhà mới bố trí phòng gì ở mỗi tầng thứ năm? Viết không quá 3 từ.
questions.explanation_en: Paragraph C describes a small garden and a children’s room on every fifth floor.
questions.explanation_vi: Đoạn C: “a small garden and a children’s room on every fifth floor”. Lưu ý: chỉ chép số từ được yêu cầu, không thêm từ không cần thiết.

questions.prompt_en: According to the survey, what two things mainly decided residents’ energy bills? Write insulation and ONE OTHER WORD.
questions.prompt_vi: Ngoài cách nhiệt, yếu tố nào quyết định hóa đơn năng lượng? Viết không quá 2 từ.
questions.explanation_en: Paragraph D says that bills mainly depended on insulation and window design.
questions.explanation_vi: Đoạn D: “depended mainly on insulation and window design”. Lưu ý: chỉ chép số từ được yêu cầu, không thêm từ không cần thiết.

questions.prompt_en: Residents’ sense of community depended more on nearby facilities than on building height.
questions.prompt_vi: Cảm giác cộng đồng phụ thuộc nhiều vào tiện ích lân cận hơn chiều cao tòa nhà.
options: TRUE
FALSE
NOT GIVEN
questions.explanation_en: TRUE: Paragraph B reports that proximity of facilities was a stronger factor than building height.
questions.explanation_vi: Đoạn B: kết quả khác nhau “less by the height of the building than by what surrounded it”.

questions.prompt_en: Most parents in the oldest estate let their children play outside alone.
questions.prompt_vi: Đa số phụ huynh ở khu nhà cũ để con chơi ngoài trời một mình.
options: TRUE
FALSE
NOT GIVEN
questions.explanation_en: FALSE: Paragraph C states that parents rarely let children play outside alone.
questions.explanation_vi: Đoạn C: họ “rarely let them play outside alone”.

questions.prompt_en: The estate with single-glazed windows was the most expensive to build.
questions.prompt_vi: Khu có kính một lớp là công trình tốn chi phí xây dựng nhất.
options: TRUE
FALSE
NOT GIVEN
questions.explanation_en: NOT GIVEN: Single glazing and heating costs are discussed, but no construction-cost ranking appears.
questions.explanation_vi: Đoạn D nói chi phí sưởi ấm cao hơn, không nói chi phí xây dựng.

questions.prompt_en: The researchers already know that the new planning rules have improved communities.
questions.prompt_vi: Nhà nghiên cứu đã biết chắc quy hoạch mới giúp gắn kết cộng đồng.
options: TRUE
FALSE
NOT GIVEN
questions.explanation_en: FALSE: Paragraph E explicitly says the impact of the new rules is not yet known.
questions.explanation_vi: Đoạn E: “Whether these rules will create stronger communities is not yet known”.

exercises.title: Reading extension: Why some new districts feel empty

instruction.en: Answer the questions after reading R-C.
instruction.vi: Đọc bài R-C và trả lời theo bằng chứng.

questions.prompt_en: According to paragraph A, why does low street life matter?
questions.prompt_vi: Theo đoạn A, vì sao đường phố ít hoạt động là vấn đề?
options: A. It makes roads wider and more expensive.
B. It affects safety, local shops and social contact.
C. It increases the number of cars in older centres.
D. It reduces the size of apartment blocks.

accepted: B. It affects safety, local shops and social contact.

questions.explanation_en: Paragraph A links empty streets to lower perceived safety, struggling shops and fewer social encounters; only option B includes all three.
questions.explanation_vi: Đoạn A nêu ba hậu quả: kém an toàn, cửa hàng khó tồn tại, ít cơ hội gặp nhau.

questions.prompt_en: What does the writer say about the separation of uses?
questions.prompt_vi: Tác giả nhận xét gì về việc tách riêng khu nhà ở, làm việc và mua sắm?
options: A. It encouraged people to walk between zones.
B. It was common in older city centres.
C. It made most journeys depend on cars.
D. It was introduced in the twenty-first century.

accepted: C. It made most journeys depend on cars.

questions.explanation_en: Paragraph B explains that separated land uses made almost every journey require a car, matching option C.
questions.explanation_vi: Đoạn B: “almost every trip required a car” – paraphrase của đáp án C.

questions.prompt_en: What is true about the link between small blocks and walking?
questions.prompt_vi: Điều gì đúng về mối quan hệ giữa ô phố ngắn và việc đi bộ?
options: A. It is equally strong in every country.
B. It has been found, but it is affected by other factors.
C. It has never been studied outside one country.
D. It shows that long blocks are safer.

accepted: B. It has been found, but it is affected by other factors.

questions.explanation_en: Paragraph C links small blocks with walking but qualifies the link by climate and income; option B preserves that qualification.
questions.explanation_vi: Đoạn C: “linked … although the strength of this link varies with climate and income”.

questions.prompt_en: Why do some developers open shops and bus routes early?
questions.prompt_vi: Vì sao một số chủ đầu tư mở cửa hàng và tuyến xe buýt sớm?
options: A. To sell homes at a higher price.
B. To finish the district in one stage.
C. To stop residents forming car-based habits.
D. To meet a government deadline.

accepted: C. To stop residents forming car-based habits.

questions.explanation_en: Paragraph D says travel habits form early and are difficult to change; shops and buses are introduced early to avoid car-based habits.
questions.explanation_vi: Đoạn D: thói quen đi lại hình thành sớm và khó thay đổi; mở dịch vụ trước để khu phố “working … from the start”.

questions.prompt_en: What name do planners give to the problem of empty streets? Write NO MORE THAN THREE WORDS.
questions.prompt_vi: Các nhà quy hoạch gọi hiện tượng phố vắng người là gì? Viết không quá 3 từ.
questions.explanation_en: Paragraph A directly calls the problem “low street life”.
questions.explanation_vi: Đoạn A: “They call it low street life”. Lưu ý: chỉ chép số từ được yêu cầu, không thêm từ không cần thiết.

questions.prompt_en: In older centres, where are homes often placed? Write NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS.
questions.prompt_vi: Trong trung tâm đô thị cũ, nhà ở thường nằm ở đâu? Viết không quá 2 từ.
questions.explanation_en: Paragraph B describes “homes above shops” in traditional mixed-use centres.
questions.explanation_vi: Đoạn B: “mix homes above shops”. Lưu ý: chỉ chép số từ được yêu cầu, không thêm từ không cần thiết.

questions.prompt_en: What can short blocks create more of, as well as corners and routes? Write NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS.
questions.prompt_vi: Ngoài nhiều góc và tuyến đường, ô phố ngắn tạo thêm loại điểm nào? Viết không quá 2 từ.
questions.explanation_en: Paragraph C lists “more corners, more crossing points and more routes”.
questions.explanation_vi: Đoạn C: “more corners, more crossing points and more routes”. Lưu ý: chỉ chép số từ được yêu cầu, không thêm từ không cần thiết.

questions.prompt_en: Which spaces have councils allowed markets to use at weekends? Write NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS.
questions.prompt_vi: Hội đồng cho phép chợ cuối tuần sử dụng khu vực nào? Viết không quá 2 từ.
questions.explanation_en: Paragraph E states that councils let weekend markets use car parks.
questions.explanation_vi: Đoạn E: “allowed markets to use car parks at weekends”. Lưu ý: chỉ chép số từ được yêu cầu, không thêm từ không cần thiết.

instruction.en: Choose the closest meaning in the context of the passage.
instruction.vi: Chọn cách diễn đạt đồng nghĩa theo ngữ cảnh.

questions.prompt_en: Which phrase is closest in meaning to “almost every trip required a car”?
questions.prompt_vi: Cụm nào gần nghĩa nhất với “hầu như mọi chuyến đi cần ô tô”?
options: most journeys depended on driving
few drivers owned cars
all roads were closed
questions.explanation_en: The sentence indicates car dependence, not car ownership or road closure.
questions.explanation_vi: Câu mô tả sự phụ thuộc ô tô, không nói quyền sở hữu hay đóng đường.

questions.prompt_en: Which phrase best paraphrases “within walking distance”?
questions.prompt_vi: Cụm nào gần nghĩa nhất với “trong khoảng cách đi bộ được”?
options: near enough to reach on foot
only accessible by train
far from local homes

accepted: near enough to reach on foot

questions.explanation_en: Walking distance means close enough to travel without a vehicle.
questions.explanation_vi: Walking distance là khoảng cách đủ gần để đi bộ.

questions.prompt_en: Which is the best paraphrase for “it varies with climate and income”?
questions.prompt_vi: Câu nào diễn đạt tương đương “thay đổi theo khí hậu và thu nhập”?
options: its strength depends partly on the weather and earnings
it is always the same everywhere
it is caused entirely by high income

accepted: its strength depends partly on the weather and earnings

questions.explanation_en: The phrase describes factors that can change a relationship, not an absolute rule.
questions.explanation_vi: Cụm nói quan hệ phụ thuộc yếu tố, không phải quy luật tuyệt đối.

questions.prompt_en: Which expression means “an association, not proof of cause”?
questions.prompt_vi: Cụm nào nghĩa là “có liên quan nhưng không chứng minh nguyên nhân”?
options: a link without demonstrated causation
a guaranteed direct effect
an unrelated observation
questions.explanation_en: Association differs from proof that one thing caused another.
questions.explanation_vi: Mối liên hệ không đồng nghĩa quan hệ nhân quả.

instruction.en: Fill the sentence from R-B or R-C using NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS.
instruction.vi: Hoàn thành câu theo bài R-B hoặc R-C, không quá 2 từ.

questions.prompt_en: Traditional centres often have homes ____ ____.
questions.prompt_vi: Các trung tâm truyền thống có nhà ở ____ các cửa hàng.
questions.explanation_en: Paragraph B states “homes above shops”.
questions.explanation_vi: Đoạn B nêu homes above shops.

questions.prompt_en: The original article says that almost every trip required ____ ____.
questions.prompt_vi: Bài đọc nói gần như mỗi chuyến đi đều cần ____ ____.
questions.explanation_en: Paragraph B uses the exact phrase “required a car”.
questions.explanation_vi: Đoạn B sử dụng đúng cụm required a car.

questions.prompt_en: Residents have fewer chances to ____ each other.
questions.prompt_vi: Cư dân có ít cơ hội ____ nhau hơn.
questions.explanation_en: Paragraph A says “residents have fewer chances to meet one another”.
questions.explanation_vi: Đoạn A nói residents have fewer chances to meet one another.
